recipes.name: Cheesy Potato and Corn Chowder
ingredients_raw: 1 (2.5 ounce) package country style gravy mix
1 cup shredded Mexican-style processed cheese food

steps.text: Melt margarine in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add celery and onion; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes. Add chicken broth; bring to a boil. Add potatoes and reduce heat to low; cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are soft, 20 to 25 minutes.

Stir in corn and chiles; increase heat to medium-high and return to a boil. Dissolve gravy mix in milk in a bowl; stir into boiling chowder. Stir in cheese and reduce heat to low; cook and stir until cheese is melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Potato and Corn Chowder
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy potato and corn chowder recipe simmers country-style milk gravy mix, veggies, and chicken broth with Mexican-style cheese and green chiles.

review.reviewBody:
this was scrumpious. 
what we did was fry about half lb. bacon drain some fat then fry onions,celery,carrots and chilis in that .
than add broth and potatoes cook till tender and stir in cheese and some cream and milk and 1 can corn and 2 cans cream corn . 
served it in big soup bowls topped with the bacon crumbled . 
everybody loved it little ones to oldest .
 is a keeper 
***************************************

even thou its summer still make this soup
i fry up few slices bacon then cook veggies in some a the bacon drippings then put carrots ,onions ,celery and chilis in crockpot with chicken broth add potatoes and corn and cook on low about 6 hrs till potatoes tender then add the creamed corn, milk and cream.
and cook about 1/2 hr and then add the cheese and let it melt into the soup .
we have it in bowls topped with the crumbled bacon even in hot weather with crockpot it doesnt heat up kitchen

The sausage gravy just makes the dish! We had lots of veggies, so at the "add potatos" stage, I also added diced carrots and some cauliflower. My extra touch was using my Cuisenart handheld and puréed 60% of it before adding the milk and corn. ;)

I loved this recipe! I added more potatoes thus adding more chicken broth. I also added about a 1/2 cup carrots and 3 cloves of garlic in the beginning, with the celery and onion. Additionally, I wanted to add some extra protein so I added 1lb of sausage. 

All in all, this always super yummy. I served it with some fresh made biscuits.

Very Good made exactly as written. With two small changes, this might be the best pot of soup I've ever made!! Instead of regular country gravy mix, I used 1/2!! of a 2.75oz package of Pioneer Brand SAUSAGE country gravy mix. It does not have sausage bits. As finished soup simmers, add 1/2 cup white wine or more to taste. I used Savignon Blanc. But any acid addition could be used, ie. lemon juice or even a small amount of rice wine or apple cider vinegar. It definitely needs the acid. I like to brown the onions and celery in bacon fat first and be sure to add salt when potatoes are added to the broth. Potatoes, like pasta have to cook in the salt or, no matter how much salt you add after cooking, they'll never have flavor. 
Yes, this recipe has lots of fat but for special occasions, this can't be beat. Outstanding!!

Made it. Didn't have celery so omitted. Not a big bacon fan so used some bacon fat while cooking onions and used cut pieces of ham. Used a fresh jalapeno small diced and fresh corn off cob. Cooked whole cobs in broth to add extra flavor. Less milk mostly about 1 C half n half. Lots of cheese at end in soup for more cheesy soup.

My husband asked for a second bowl!
I didn't have the gravy mix, so I made a roux ( 1/4 cup butter and 1/4 cup flour) and reduced the milk to one cup. I will definitely be making this again and will add some crispy bacon as other reviewers have recommended.

I made this in a little different order because one of my kids doesn’t like corn. So I followed the recipe until the potatoes were cooked. Then added the gravy/milk mixture. Then separated into two pots. I added Soutwestern corn and diced green Chili’s to one pot. I added shredded sharp cheddar to both pots (I forgot I had Velveeta). Both versions needed a little salt & pepper, but were very good. Now I have a good base for a potato cheese soup in addition to corn chowder.

Absolutely a soup to make on a chilly fall day . I will be using the base of the chowder for my fish chowder for sure. I would put two cups of potatoes and two cups of out right from the garden corn next time. you can take corn right off the cob without cooking and freeze it in you Food Saver bags...cook as you would when you buy frozen at the store

I made this without the cheese. I added chopped asparagus at the halfway point of cooking the potatoes too. When complete I put about half the soup in an immersion blender, which considerably thickened it. It also screamed for black pepper and I added some at the end.

It makes a very hearty soup. Perfect for a cold day.

This is SO GOOD! Added about a tablespoon of minced garlic when cooking onion and celery. Also added 1/8 teaspoon of cayenne pepper and 1 teaspoon of crushed red pepper. Then added 3 strips of crushed bacon. Served with green onion and bacon crumbles on top and garlic cheese biscuits on the side. It was really a good combo!

Incredibly easy to make! I prepared as instructed (but did add leftover ham), only change was putting all ingredients in crock pot before potatoes were fully cooked and cooking on low 8 hours. OMG awesome, my family loved it and now wants it to be our traditional NYE dinner!

I scaled this back to make two servings. I had to make a couple modifications based on what I had available, and didn't have country gravy mix, so I added a little more butter to the pan and once the onions and celery were softened, I added a little flour and made a roux then added the milk to that and made gravy. I did add some black pepper to it as it cooked to mimic country style pepper gravy. Chicken bouillon powder and water made broth. I used a leftover baked potato and cut it into cubes and added it in with the corn. Diced roasted Hatch chiles worked out great in this right from the jar. I only had plain Velveeta, but I added a sprinkle of dried crushed jalapeno and a dash of cayenne to make it "mexican" cheese. I did let this simmer for a little while to let those flavors develop. This has some heat from that spice. I'd rate it medium. It leaves a little lingering warmth but not a bitter afterburn. Very nice soup. This was a great way to use up a few leftovers too!
I've add this to the menu for wedding and baby showers. Always a hit! I've never changed anything. It's perfect as is!

I make this every fall, and have for as long as I remember. It's so good, so simple, and the only change I make is to use frozen corn instead of canned. Otherwise, this is my go-to "it's finally fall!" recipe. I love it.

This was great on a cold, Spring day. This is such a versatile recipe. I made as directed but only had a package of the Pioneer gravy mix that was somewhat larger ( 2 plus oz.). By using that I didn’t need the milk that was called for. We do enjoy a thicker soup though so I could see using the milk for something thinner.

I used this recipe about 2 years ago, for the first time. It was fantastic. I did omit the celery and substituted onion powder for the onion. It was a hit. Today is the first time that I didn't have to worry about pleasing picky eaters. I followed it to a tee, and it is so full of flavor. WOW! Is all I can say. And thank you for a great recipe.
Easy to make and enjoyable.
Have used it many times. My niece borrowed my copy to make soup at her college’s laboratory sciences class soup contest & her group won 1st place.

I usually follow a recipe to the letter, this time I did add a small amount of bacon. That is the only change I made. But this chowder was fantastic! I will absolutely be making this again. And am planning to share with friends for a very together this weekend as well. They are gluten free so I bought a package of pioneer gf country gravy and expect just as great results. Love this stuff.
Super fast to make. I always have the ingredients on hand. Absolutely delicious!
